DECISIONS

Source: DECISIONS.md

One dated entry per decision. M0 evidence came from spikes/, deleted in M1 (recover it from the first commit in git history); M1+ evidence lives in tests/testthat/. Re-run the relevant spike or test when bumping shiny or plumber.

Environment for all M0 entries: R 4.5.2, Ubuntu 26.04.1, shiny 1.14.0, plumber 1.3.3 (CRAN), httpuv 1.6.17, whisker 0.4.1, htmltools 0.5.9, promises 1.5.0, future 1.70.0, chromote 0.5.1, Chrome for Testing (chrome-headless-shell) 155.0.8059.79.

2026-10-15 — M0 step 0: environment and browser for e2e tests

  • plumber 1.3.3 was already installed (PLAN §4.0 said it was not). chromote 0.5.1 was installed from CRAN.
  • Browser: chromote::local_chrome_version("latest-stable", binary = "chrome-headless-shell") downloads Chrome for Testing into ~/.cache/R/chromote/chrome/. No system Chrome is used. CI uses the same call in a setup step, so local runs and CI run the same binary.
  • Sandbox: Ubuntu 23.10+ sets kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1, so Chrome aborts with FATAL ... No usable sandbox!. The fix is chromote::set_chrome_args(c(chromote::default_chrome_args(), "--no-sandbox")). This is acceptable because the browser only loads our own localhost test app. helper-chrome.R applies it on Linux. The alternative needs root: an AppArmor profile for the downloaded binary.
  • Name check: spigot is not on CRAN or in the CRAN archive, and no R repo of that name turned up on GitHub. (Spigot is also a well-known Minecraft server project, so web searches are noisy, but there is no R-package conflict.)

2026-10-15 — M0 step 1: mount via app$httpHandler (spikes/01-mount.R)

  • GET, POST (JSON echo), PUT and DELETE all reach plumber through the wrapped httpHandler over real httpuv. Shiny still serves /. F1, F3 confirmed.
  • A wrong verb on an existing path gives 405. F14 confirmed.
  • After stripping /api from PATH_INFO = "/api", the result is "". Mapping "" to "/" makes /api and /api/ both hit GET /. plumber sees PATH_INFO = "/pathinfo" (prefix gone), with the prefix moved to SCRIPT_NAME.
  • Calling rook.input$read() before pr$call() without a rewind makes plumber see an empty body ([]). After rewind() it recovers ({"a":[1]}). Rule: never pre-read; if you must, rewind. F13 confirmed.
  • plumber’s default serializer boxes scalars ({"root":[true]}). This confirms that spigot_api() must install a spigot_json()-compatible serializer (M1 step 8).

2026-10-15 — M0 step 2: promise returned from httpHandler (spikes/02-promise.R)

  • GET /slow returns promises::future_promise({Sys.sleep(2); ...}) under multisession. The wrapper returns then(pr$call(req), rook_to_httpResponse). Result: 200 {"ok":[true]} after 2.16 s, and a concurrent GET /api/ completed in 8 ms while /slow was pending. F4 confirmed; the process is not blocked.
  • Test-harness gotcha: the first attempt used curl::curl_fetch_multi on one pool. Both requests finished at ~2.4 s because the client serialised them. Concurrency tests must issue the slow request from a separate process (callr::r_bg), or use separate connections. M1 integration test 5 must follow this.

2026-10-15 — M0 step 3: session token on the JS side (spikes/03-token.R)

  • Shiny.shinyapp.config.sessionId === session$token in 5/5 tabs. The token is 32 lowercase hex chars. F7 confirmed.
  • Correction to PLAN (§3, M3 step 1/9): config.sessionId is not set at shiny:connected. It arrives in the server’s config message, about 2–6 ms later. shiny.js sets this.config and then triggers shiny:sessioninitialized in the same handler (shiny.js 1.14.0 l. 6955–6963). In all 5 runs: undefined at shiny:connected, defined at shiny:sessioninitialized.
  • Decision: spigot.ready resolves on shiny:sessioninitialized. If the script runs after that event has fired, it resolves immediately when Shiny.shinyapp.config.sessionId is already set. (Shiny.initializedPromise also exists in 1.14.0, but it is not documented public API, so we do not depend on it.)
  • Timing: the token is available about 9–15 ms after DOMContentLoaded on localhost.

2026-10-15 — M0 step 4: whisker page + Shiny deps (spikes/04-page.R)

  • Approach adopted as specified in PLAN §4.3:
    1. Render the full template with whisker (partials included).
    2. Split the rendered output once at the first </head>, matched case-insensitively.
    3. Pass the two halves as HTML() into the fixed template "{{ head }}{{ headContent() }}</head>{{ rest }}" with document_ = TRUE.
  • Results in Chrome: exactly 1 shiny script and 1 jQuery, both inside <head>. One <head> and one <body>. Shiny connects. <HEAD> in uppercase works. lang is kept. Non-ASCII (Größe – ✓) round-trips. Items and partials render.
  • Injection test: data = list(title = "{{ Sys.getenv('HOME') }}") renders literally, via both {{ }} and {{{ }}}. $HOME appears nowhere in the response. Negative control: option B (htmlTemplate(text_ = whisker_output)) does evaluate it, so option B stays rejected.
  • Split rule: split the rendered output, not the template. That way a </head> inside a partial (e.g. {{> head}}) works. A triple-stache value containing </head> could move the split. That is not an escalation: {{{ }}} already means “raw HTML”, and both halves are HTML(), so nothing gets re-templated. At render time, no </head> → error. At construction time, spigot_page() errors if neither the template nor any partial contains </head>.
  • Shiny adds its own <meta http-equiv="Content-Type" ...> after the user’s head content. A duplicate charset meta is harmless.

2026-10-15 — M0 step 5: reactive bridge latency (spikes/05-trigger.R)

50 sequential iterations in headless Chrome against localhost, after 5 warm-up iterations:

Leg median p95 max
HTTP round-trip (fetch POST /api/tick) 3.1 ms 3.4 ms 5.5 ms
fetch start → spigot:set-input received 2.6 ms 3.7 ms 33.0 ms
set-input → pong (setInputValue → observer → message) 41.8 ms 43.1 ms 44.7 ms
fetch resolve → pong (decision metric) 41.3 ms 42.7 ms 74.1 ms
Baseline: plain Shiny.setInputValue → observer → pong, no HTTP 42.2 ms 43.1 ms 44.6 ms
  • Decision: option 1 (round-trip via spigot:set-input) adopted; option 2 closed. p95 of 42.7 ms is under 50 ms.
  • The ~40 ms floor is Shiny’s own input → observer → output path: the plain-Shiny baseline is the same. The bridge adds only the push leg (~3 ms), so option 2 would not have removed the floor.
  • The push message arrived before fetch resolved in 5/50 cases. Server pushes go out during the handler, before the HTTP response. Client code must not assume HTTP-response-then-push ordering. This goes in the reactivity vignette.
  • M6 regression bound (5 × spike p95): trigger latency median < 215 ms.

2026-10-15 — M1: httpuv static paths answer API POSTs with 400 (F16)

  • Found by the M1 integration fixture, which is an app directory with www/. Every API POST returned plain-text 400 Bad Request, while GET worked. The M0 spikes missed this because they ran shinyApp() objects, which have no static path at /.
  • Cause: shinyAppDir() registers www/ as an httpuv static path at / (fallthrough). httpuv answers non-GET requests under a static path itself, on its I/O thread, before R sees them. Shiny excludes its own /session with excludeStaticPath() for the same reason. startHttpuvApp() builds the static paths from the outer appobj, so the inner appobj returned by app.R cannot add an exclusion. This affects every deployed app dir with www/ (Shiny Server, Connect).
  • Decision: mount_app() wraps onStart. It calls later::later() to run getShinyOption("server")$setStaticPath(<prefix> = excludeStaticPath()) on the first event-loop tick. onStart runs before the httpuv server exists; shinyOptions(server =) is set right after it. Shiny’s exported addResourcePath() uses the same server handle, and WebServer$setStaticPath() is public httpuv API. Scratch check: without the fix POST → 400; with it POST/GET → 200 and www/ files are still served. This also keeps a www/api/ folder from shadowing API GETs.
  • Residual window: a non-GET API request that arrives between listen() and the first loop tick still gets 400. Page loads go through the same later queue, behind the exclusion, so a browser cannot hit this window. With M2’s require_session = TRUE an API call needs a loaded page, so the window is closed in practice.
  • Regression guard: test-mount.R integration tests (fixture apps/mount/ has www/).

2026-10-15 — M1: plumber binds the default serializer at endpoint creation (F17)

  • pr$handle() (and so pr_get() etc.) copies private$default_serializer into the endpoint when the endpoint is created. Endpoints parsed from a file without @serializer store NULL and use the router default at request time.
  • So pr$setSerializer() after pr() |> pr_get(...) has no effect on those endpoints. The M1 step 8 plan (set the serializer on a router passed in) could not work.
  • Decision: spigot_api(file = NULL). NULL returns an empty router that already has the spigot_json() serializer, so routers built in code start from it: spigot_api() |> pr_get(...). A file path → pr(file) + serializer (works, see above). A Plumber object is returned unchanged and not mutated: its endpoints keep their serializers. spigot_app(api = <Plumber>) uses it as given.

2026-10-15 — M1: request env fidelity and mount details

  • httpuv sets both CONTENT_TYPE and HTTP_CONTENT_TYPE (and both CONTENT_LENGTH forms), plus HEADERS (named, lowercase) and REMOTE_PORT. plumber reads HTTP_CONTENT_TYPE. fake_req() mirrors this (checked against a live httpuv request).
  • Binary request bodies need parsers = "octet" on the endpoint. plumber’s default parser set falls back to text, and rawToChar() fails on NUL bytes (500). This is ordinary plumber usage; the getting-started vignette should mention it.
  • spigot_mount_handler() forces fallback. Otherwise mount_app()’s fallback = app$httpHandler is a lazy promise, first evaluated after the field is replaced, so the handler calls itself (node stack overflow, seen as Shiny’s HTML 500 on GET /).
  • The rewritten PATH_INFO/SCRIPT_NAME are restored when the request finishes. For async results that is in promises::finally(), not on.exit(), because plumber routes after async filters resolve. Test: “the prefix stays stripped until an async filter has finished routing”.
  • Mount-level failures (sync or async) → {"error":"internal server error"} 500. The condition message goes to stderr via message() and never to the client.
  • Prefix rule: ^(/[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+)+$. The first segment must not be session or shared (Shiny serves both itself).

2026-10-15 — M2: integration tests open Shiny sessions without a browser

  • open_session(url) (helper-server.R) connects a websocket::WebSocket to /websocket/ and sends {"method":"init","data":{}}. Shiny answers {"config":{"workerId":"","sessionId":"<token>","user":null}} on connect, runs the server function after init, and then flushes {"errors":{},"values":{},...}. The helper waits for that flush, so the session is registered before the first API call. Closing the socket fires onSessionEnded (scratch check: START/END both logged).
  • So session integration tests (401/200, token dies with the session, 413) need no Chrome. Chrome is only used for what needs a real browser: the Origin header a browser POST sends, and closing a tab. websocket (already a chromote dependency) and chromote are in Suggests.
  • helper-chrome.R does not download. It uses a browser on the PATH, else the cached Chrome for Testing headless shell (chromote::chrome_versions_list("installed")). It skips with the install command when neither exists.

2026-10-15 — M2: session registry and server wrapper

  • One process-global registry (.registry, token → session). A token from another spigot app in the same R process would be accepted by this app’s API. Deployed apps run one app per process (Shiny Server, Connect, runApp), so this is accepted for now. Revisit if spigot_broadcast() (M4) needs per-app scope.
  • register_session() is idempotent: a second call for the same session adds no second onSessionEnded callback. Removal only deletes the entry if it is still that session.
  • lookup_session() also treats session$isClosed() as gone. This covers any gap between the socket closing and onSessionEnded running.
  • wrap_server() always has formals (input, output, session) and calls the user’s function with the arguments Shiny would give it. It mirrors shiny:::argsForServerFunc(): session and clientData only when named in its formals; ... does not receive them. F20.

2026-10-15 — M2: origin guard rules

  • Origin is used when present, else Referer. With neither, the request passes (same-origin GET).
  • The source’s scheme://authority is compared, case-insensitively, with Host and with every entry of X-Forwarded-Host (comma-separated). :80 is dropped for http and :443 for https on both sides. Origin: null, userinfo (user@host), non-URLs, and a source with no Host to compare against → 403.
  • Accepting X-Forwarded-Host does not weaken the guard. A cross-site page cannot set that header without a CORS preflight, and the API never answers a preflight with CORS headers. Likewise, a cross-site fetch cannot send X-Spigot-Session without a preflight. So with require_session = TRUE the session check alone already blocks CSRF, and the origin guard is defence in depth. With require_session = FALSE it is the only CSRF guard.
  • Not verified here (no deployment on this machine): whether Shiny Server and Posit Connect keep Host or set X-Forwarded-Host. If a proxy rewrites Host and sets neither, every browser POST gets 403. Check this on a real deployment before M7. PLAN §7 Q6 (allow_origins) is the escape hatch.
  • The origin check runs before the session check: a cross-origin request gets 403 even with a valid token.

2026-10-15 — M2: max_request_size defaults to NULL (changes PLAN §3)

  • PLAN §3 had max_request_size = 5 * 1024^2. That would silently override an options(shiny.maxRequestSize = ...) the user set themselves. Decision: default NULL leaves the option alone (Shiny’s own default is 5 MB). A number sets it in onStart. shiny::onStop() (registered inside onStart, so it is app-level) restores the old value. Inf means no limit. Values <= 0 are rejected, though Shiny would read them as unlimited.
  • Shiny’s httpuv onHeaders reads the option per request, so setting it in onStart works. A body with Transfer-Encoding and no Content-Length counts as size Inf, so it always gets 413 while any finite limit is set. F19.
  • The 413 body is Shiny’s plain text (Maximum upload size exceeded). This is documented in the spigot_app() “Request size” section, which is the draft for the vignette note.

2026-10-15 — M2: the minimal example sends the token itself until M3

  • require_session = TRUE is the default, so inst/examples/minimal/www/app.js now waits for shiny:sessioninitialized and sends X-Spigot-Session. spigot.js (M3) will replace this.
  • Gotcha caught by the e2e test: the script’s own const $ = (id) => ... shadows jQuery’s $ across the whole script (temporal dead zone). Use jQuery(document) explicitly.

2026-10-15 — M3: how spigot.js learns the prefix (changes PLAN M3 step 10)

  • PLAN had spigot_dependency() set window.__spigot = {prefix} with the dependency’s head field. htmltools’ renderDependencies() writes head after the dependency’s <script>, so the global would not exist yet when spigot.js runs.
  • Decision: the script tag carries it, <script src=".../spigot.js" data-prefix="/api"> (script = list(src, data-prefix); htmltools ≥ 0.5 renders attribute lists). spigot.js reads document.currentScript. No inline script, so it also works under a CSP without unsafe-inline. The prefix goes through check_prefix(), which only admits [A-Za-z0-9._~-] segments, so it cannot break out of the attribute.
  • spigot_app() wraps ui in attach_spigot(), a function(req) that calls the user’s ui the way Shiny does (ui(req) if it has formals, else ui()), passes an httpResponse through, and attachDependencies(append = TRUE)s the rest. Shiny puts jQuery and shiny.js first, so spigot.js always loads after them (asserted in test-client.R).
  • Gotcha caught by the integration test: attach_spigot() must force(ui). spigot_app() does ui <- attach_spigot(ui, ...), so an unforced promise evaluates to the wrapper itself and the page fails with “infinite recursion”. A unit test now reproduces the reassignment.

2026-10-15 — M3: spigot.js behaviour

  • spigot.base = prefix (leading slash dropped) + /, resolved against document.baseURI, so it is the API next to the page. Writable. Paths have leading slashes stripped. A request’s URL is fixed when the call is made, even if it then waits for ready.
  • For M5: a page at a nested path (/docs/intro) would resolve api/ to /docs/api/. Shiny’s own relative dependency URLs (shared/shiny.min.js) break the same way there, so nested pages need a <base href> to the app root anyway; spigot.base follows it with no change.
  • spigot.ready resolves on shiny:sessioninitialized (M0 step 3), or immediately if the token is already set. The header value is read from Shiny.shinyapp.config.sessionId at send time, so after a Shiny reconnect requests use the new token. The header is set last: options.headers cannot override it (any case).
  • Bodies: FormData, Blob, URLSearchParams, ArrayBuffer/views and ReadableStream are sent unchanged; everything else, strings included, is JSON with Content-Type: application/json. A string sent raw would arrive as text/plain, which plumber does not parse as JSON; text goes in a Blob. Accept: application/json by default.
  • Replies: empty → null; Content-Type */json or *+json that parses → the value; anything else → text. Non-2xx → SpigotError(status, message, body), message = the JSON error field if it is a string, else statusText, else HTTP <status>. No reply → status 0: "... timed out after <n> ms" or "... failed: network error (...)".
  • timeout counts from the call (including any wait for ready), then aborts the fetch via AbortController. The e2e test checks the fetch’s signal.aborted. No default timeout yet; PLAN §4.6 spigot_options(timeout =) will supply one.
  • SpigotError is ES5-style (Object.create(Error.prototype)), so instanceof Error holds. It lives at spigot.SpigotError, not on window.
  • spigot.on/off and the spigot:event / spigot:set-input handlers (PLAN M3 step 9) are not in M3. They are written in M4 and M6 with the tests that cover them.

2026-10-15 — M3: subpath test proxy

  • helper-proxy.R start_proxy() runs a reverse proxy in a callr process: httpuv runServer() for HTTP (forwarded with a synchronous curl call) and websockets (bridged to a websocket::WebSocket client, messages buffered until the upstream opens). It strips /sub/app, and like nginx defaults it rewrites Host to the upstream and sets X-Forwarded-Host.
  • So the e2e test also proves, with a real browser POST, that the origin guard accepts X-Forwarded-Host behind a proxy that rewrites Host. Whether Shiny Server and Posit Connect behave like this proxy is still unverified (M2 entry).
  • Gotcha: callr read_all_output_lines() blocks until the process exits; use read_output_lines() to peek at a live proxy.

2026-10-15 — 401 responses carry a hint

  • Calling the API by hand (curl, Postman) against an app with require_session = TRUE gave a bare {"error":"session required"}. The 401 body is now {"error": "session required", "hint": "You may be interested in spigot_app(..., require_session = FALSE)."}. error is unchanged, so SpigotError.message in spigot.js is the same.
  • The hint is deliberately terse and the same for every 401: it points a developer at the setting so they can troubleshoot from the docs, and says nothing about tokens, the header, or how to borrow a live tab’s session. A first draft that explained all of that was rejected as too strong a pointer for a caller who should not be using the API.
  • It still tells any caller that the server is a spigot app. Accepted: nothing secret is revealed.

2026-10-15 — M4: push

  • ShinySession$sendCustomMessage() writes to the websocket immediately (shiny 1.14.0: sendMessage() → write() → websocket$send()), not at the next flush, and silently does nothing once the session is closed. So an endpoint can emit without a reactive context, and an event can reach the page before the endpoint’s HTTP reply (as M0 step 5 measured).
  • Message: sendCustomMessage("spigot:event", list(event, json)), where json is a plain string from spigot_json(), so Shiny’s own toJSON() (different dataframe/digits settings) never shapes the payload. spigot.js JSON.parses it. spigot_broadcast() serialises once for all sessions.
  • spigot_emit(NULL, ...) warns and returns FALSE (an endpoint run with require_session = FALSE and no token). A non-session object errors. Event names: any non-empty string, in R and JS.
  • spigot_broadcast() sends to every session in the registry, skipping and pruning any that isClosed() or whose send throws, silently: a closed-socket race is expected, not an error. It returns the number reached. Scope: the registry is process-global (M2 entry), so broadcast reaches every spigot app’s sessions in this R process. Kept: deployments run one app per process. Revisit with a per-app registry only if that changes.
  • JS: spigot.on(event, fn) returns an unsubscribe function; adding the same fn twice is a no-op (as addEventListener); spigot.off(event) with no fn removes all of that event’s listeners. Listeners run on a copy of the list, so one may off itself mid-dispatch. A throwing listener does not stop the rest; its error is rethrown in a setTimeout, so it still reaches the console and window.onerror, as a DOM listener’s error does. Listeners get (data, event) with this === spigot.
  • spigot_broadcast(except =, filter =), added for multi-user pages (one tab’s action updates the others; chat rooms). except: a session or list of sessions, compared by identity after rootScope(), because a module’s session is a session_proxy that is never identical() to the registered root (Shiny’s real proxy is used in the test). filter(session) must return TRUE/FALSE; it runs for every open session before any send, so a failing filter sends nothing rather than half a broadcast. Rooms are just filter over session$userData; a spigot_join()/room = API waits for a real need.
  • Multi-user reach is one R process. Open-source Shiny Server runs one process per app; Posit Connect can start several (max processes / connections per process), and users in different processes do not see each other’s broadcasts. Cross-process push needs an external relay (Redis, Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY) and is out of scope. Document for M7.
  • No replay: events that arrive before the page calls spigot.on() for them are dropped.
  • The “live” vignette draft is the spigot_emit() help page (one tab vs all, shapes, push-before-reply ordering, emit from the main process not a future worker).
  • Integration tests read pushes from the websocket without Chrome: open_session() now returns custom(type).

2026-10-16 — M5: pages replaces ui, and takes Shiny UI too

  • spigot_app(pages, ...) replaces the temporary ui argument (PLAN §3). pages is one page, served at /, or a named list keyed by path. A plain (unclassed) list is a list of pages; anything classed (a spigot_page, a tagList, an html_document) or a function is one page.
  • A page is a spigot_page() or anything shinyApp() takes as ui (fluidPage(), htmlTemplate(), function(req), an httpResponse). This keeps Shiny UI available as an opt-in, per the §1 non-goals, and let every M1–M4 fixture switch from ui = to pages = with no other change.
  • spigot_page() attaches no dependency itself. spigot_app() attaches spigot_dependency() to every page in attach_spigot(), as in M3, so spigot.js is attached in one place for both kinds of page (changes PLAN M5 step 9). attach_spigot() now passes NULL through.

2026-10-16 — M5: page paths are one segment; a trailing slash redirects

Path rule superseded by “nested pages get a <base href>” below; the redirect and routing notes still hold.

  • Shiny writes its dependency URLs relative (jquery-3.7.1/jquery.min.js). A page at /docs/intro, or at /about/, resolves them under /docs/ or /about/ and loads no Shiny, so no session and no API. The M3 entry suggested a <base href>. Rejected for now: injecting one silently changes the user’s own relative links, and turns href="#section" into a link to the app root.
  • Decision: a page path is / or one segment (^/[A-Za-z0-9._~-]+$, not /session or /shared, and not under the API prefix). Nested pages are an error at spigot_app() time; support them later only if a site needs them (then <base href> is the likely answer).
  • /about/ gets 301 with Location: ../about plus the query string, instead of serving the page there (PLAN §4.3 said “normalised”). The relative Location stays correct under a proxy subpath: the e2e test opens /sub/app/about/ through start_proxy() and lands on /sub/app/about with a working session. A trailing slash on an unknown path is a 404.
  • Routing is shinyApp(uiPattern = ".*") with page_router() as the ui function (F10). Unknown paths get a fixed HTML 404 that does not echo the path. Under runApp(), shared/, every dependency directory and www/ are httpuv static paths (startHttpuvApp(), addResourcePath()), so the catch-all shadows only Shiny’s R-level handlers after the app’s: /reactlog and /reactlog/mark, which page_router() returns NULL for.
  • Only GET reaches a page (Shiny’s uiHttpHandler, F3). A POST /about gets Shiny’s 404, or httpuv’s plain-text 400 in an app directory with www/ (F16).

2026-10-16 — M5: templates

  • A template (or partial) string containing <, {{ or a line break is template text; anything else is a file path, read as UTF-8 when spigot_page() runs, relative to the working directory (the app directory under runApp()). A missing file is an error naming it. Shiny’s autoreload re-sources app.R when an .html file changes, so reading once is fine in development.
  • whisker sees only data: a global or a local variable of the same name renders empty (checked, also for {{HOME}}). It escapes &, <, >, ", not '; ?spigot_page says to use double-quoted attributes. whisker has no lambdas (a function value renders empty).
  • whisker reads <name>.mustache from the working directory for a partial it was not given. spigot does not want two sources of partials: spigot_page() checks every {{> name}} tag against partials at creation, and render_whisker() renders from an empty temp directory and turns whisker’s “No partial” warning into an error (this covers tags after a delimiter change, which the creation check cannot see).
  • </head> must be in the template or a partial at creation (M0 step 4), matched as </head\s*> in any case; a render whose output has none is an error.
  • data is a named list, or a function called per request (with req if it takes an argument, as Shiny calls ui). cache = TRUE memoises the rendered html_document on the first request and needs list data. Since list data is static, a cached and an uncached page render the same HTML; the unit test counts render_whisker() calls instead.
  • The minimal example now uses spigot_page("index.html"); its template lost {{ headContent() }}.

2026-10-16 — M5: nested pages get a <base href> (supersedes one-segment paths)

  • Nested pages matter for sites (/docs/intro), so the one-segment rule went. A path is / or one or more segments of [A-Za-z0-9._~-], with no ./.. segment, not under /session, /shared or the API prefix.
  • What breaks at depth, checked in shiny.js 1.14.0: only relative asset URLs. The websocket URL is built from location.pathname (createSocket(): pathname + / + websocket/), so a page at /about already connects to /about/websocket/, and Shiny’s server accepts any ws path but /autoreload/. Hosts that set Shiny.createSocket (Shiny Server’s SockJS, Connect) replace this; not verified on a real deployment (same caveat as the M2 origin-guard entry).
  • Decision: a spigot_page() served below the top level gets <base href="../" data-spigot> (one ../ per level, relative so it works under a proxy subpath) right after its <head> tag, before anything else in the head. Relative URLs then resolve from the app root on every page; top-level pages get no base and are unchanged. A template with its own <base> keeps it. No <head> tag at depth → render error (inserting before <!DOCTYPE> would break the page). The cache holds the HTML before the base, since one page object can be served at several depths.
  • Nested pages must be spigot_page()s. For tag-based Shiny UI, renderPage() writes Shiny’s scripts before any tags$head() content (checked), so a base added there comes too late. Error at spigot_app() time.
  • Fragment links: with a base, href="#sec" resolves to the app root (the e2e test saw the click land on /). spigot.js adds one delegated click listener: when base[data-spigot] exists, a plain left click on <a href="#..."> (no modifier, no other target, not already defaultPrevented) sets location.hash instead. Middle-click/new-tab on such a link still opens the root, and href="?tab=2" still resolves from the root; both documented in ?spigot_page.
  • Trailing slash at any depth: /docs/intro/ → 301 ../intro (plus query). // is a 404.

2026-10-16 — M6: spigot_trigger() passes the value by reference (changes PLAN §4.5, M6)

  • PLAN M6 sent the value as a spigot_json() string for the page to JSON.parse and pass to Shiny.setInputValue(). Checked in shiny 1.14.0 (shiny:::applyInputHandler()): an input with no :type whose value is an unnamed list is unlist(recursive = TRUE)ed. So I(1) arrived as 1, not a length-1 list (PLAN M6 test 5 was wrong), a data frame as one flat named vector, and NA as NULL, which a default observeEvent() (ignoreNULL = TRUE) ignores. F21.
  • Decision (Kent, 2026-10-16): by reference. spigot_trigger(session, name, value) stores value under a new id in an environment at session$userData$.spigot_triggers (hidden from ls(); a module’s session shares its root’s) and sends spigot:set-input {name, id}. spigot.js calls Shiny.setInputValue("<name>:spigot.ref", id, {priority: "event"}). The spigot.ref input handler (shiny::registerInputHandler() in .onLoad, force = TRUE) takes the id out of the store and returns the value, so input[[name]] is identical() to value: data frames, factors, Dates, NA, environments and functions included. The value never crosses the websocket, so spigot_json() is not involved.
  • An id resolves once and only in its own session; an unknown or malformed id gives NULL (an input handler cannot leave the input unset, and an error there would end the session). Ids come from a process-wide counter. Values the page never sends back (tab closed first) stay in userData until the session ends.
  • Every trigger fires the observers, same value or not: Shiny’s input is a ReactiveValues(dedupe = FALSE), and priority: "event" skips shiny.js’s client-side dedupe in InputNoResendDecorator. F22. (Ids differ anyway, but the handler’s output is what Shiny stores, so this is still what matters.)
  • name must match ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$, checked before namespacing, so no : type suffix gets through. With a module’s session, the name goes through session$ns() (the module’s input$cart). NULL session → error (unlike spigot_emit()); returns invisible(TRUE).
  • Latency is the M0 step 5 path, unchanged: the e2e test measures fetch start → observer’s pushed event over 20 sequential runs and checks the median is under 215 ms (5 × the spike’s p95). Observers run after the endpoint returns, and only while the page is open.
  • The reactivity vignette draft is ?spigot_trigger (as M4 used ?spigot_emit); M7 writes the vignette.

2026-10-16 — M7: examples

  • live: a counter shared by every tab. One endpoint uses all three channels: the HTTP reply, spigot_broadcast("count") to every tab, and spigot_trigger(s, "clicked") into the caller’s server function, which renders a Shiny text output inside the hand-written page (<div id="mine" class="shiny-text-output">). The page keeps the highest count seen, because a push can beat the reply (M0 step 5). Shared state is an environment in app.R; plumber evaluates api.R in app.R’s environment, so the endpoints see it.
  • site: three top-level pages from pages/, sharing head, nav and footer partials (a partial may hold </head>), all cache = TRUE. /cars is rendered in R with all 32 mtcars rows, then filtered through GET api/cars. POST api/fit bootstraps a slope in a future::multisession worker with future_promise(seed = TRUE) and returns both PIDs, so the test proves the work ran in another process. future stays in Suggests; the smoke test skips the example without it (needs in test-examples.R).
  • Smoke tests take (url, headers, session); session is open_session()’s, so pushes and triggers are checked without a browser. Each new example also has one chromote test.

2026-10-16 — M7: docs and pkgdown

  • Vignettes: why-spigot, getting-started (walks minimal, then site), reactivity (the three channels, the live example, concurrency), and client (the spigot.js reference, which until now was only ?spigot_dependency). Example files are shown with knitr’s embed engine from system.file("examples", ...), so the vignettes cannot drift from the shipped examples.
  • pkgdown site at https://kent-orr.github.io/spigot/, built by .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml and deployed to the gh-pages branch. “Get started” points at getting-started (pkgdown only does that by itself for a vignette named after the package).
  • PLAN §4.6 spigot_options(timeout =) was never built; spigot.js has only the per-call timeout option, and the docs say so. Deferred: no default timeout in 0.1.0.

2026-10-16 — M7: CI and the oldest shiny

  • skip_if_no_chrome() fails instead of skipping when SPIGOT_REQUIRE_CHROME=true, which the CI cells that install Chrome for Testing set (PLAN §8, “e2e silently skipped”).
  • shiny before 1.11.0 breaks hand-written forms. Its initShiny() treats any button[type=submit] on the page as a submitButton(): it calls preventDefault() on the click, so the form’s submit event never fires, and it defers every input. Fixed in shiny 1.11.0 (#4209: only .shiny-submit-button). Found by running the suite against shiny 1.8.0: the minimal and site browser tests fail and live (plain buttons) passes.
  • shiny’s httpResponse() adds X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff only from 1.14.0 (before that, X-UA-Compatible). spigot now sets nosniff itself on API responses (api_response() in rook.R).
  • Full suite (965 expectations, Chrome included) against older shiny in a scratch library: 1.8.0 and 1.10.0 fail only the minimal/site browser tests (the submit-button bug above) once nosniff is spigot’s; 1.11.0 passes everything. DESCRIPTION now has shiny (>= 1.11.0), and CI has a cell pinned to 1.11.0. F1, F4 and F9 hold back to 1.8.0.
